items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Oh, there's so many guys out there that write, too, like Phil Moore, Calvin Jackson, Benny Carter, they haven't got in yet, either.

ctx.x: I didn't know it was two different routes, you were a writer -- you was a writer, it was cool, and you get in from that end. Oh, there's so many guys out there that write, too, like Phil Moore, Calvin Jackson, Benny Carter, they haven't got in yet, either. They get a lot of studio work, to ghost write for people. That's always available for people to do.

I remember, that was the first time I saw Jimmy Knepper, he was out to Dmitri Tiomkin's (inaudible). It was a big white house on -- what street was that on? Hollywood Boulevard? A bunch of kids (inaudible) know what they were doing? They all had a little project like taking one or two bars of his music and modulating to another key for eight bars, and he'd tell you how many bars you write, and getting prepared to go to -- if you're in D flat, like, an eight-bar modulation, you go into the key of C. And you get to…
